summary: Session 2 of 2 (remediate + verify + closeout) shipped the human-locked Option-2-scoped fix for the classify-against-HomeHealthCare 240s timeout that Session 1 root-caused as a CLI process-shutdown wedge (NOT product latency). Implementation: AccessComSession now latches a process-static `ActivatedInThisProcess` flag the moment an Access COM server is activated; AccessHarvester.Cli/Program.Main routes all exits through `FinalizeExit`, which flushes stdout/stderr and calls kernel32 TerminateProcess(GetCurrentProcess(), exitCode) ONLY when that flag is set. This realizes the 'scoped to the COM-using command path(s), not every subcommand' requirement via actual COM activation rather than a subcommand-name allowlist -- tighter blast radius (parse/validate/translate/generate-docs and all usage-error early returns take the normal managed return path) and auto-covers future COM commands. Folded-in collateral fix (E5): added the DAO 'Property not found' HRESULT 0x800A0CC6 (= error 3270), captured EMPIRICALLY (all 93 degradations carried it, not inferred), to OleDbDaoSchemaReader.DaoPropertyAbsentHResults, and routed both catch...when filters through a new internal IsDaoPropertyAbsentHResult predicate exposed via InternalsVisibleTo for a hermetic test. Validation: full solution build clean; 15 hermetic tests pass (6 new HRESULT cases + 9 reaper); direct classify against HomeHealthCare exits in ~9s with exit code 0 (degradations 93 -> 0), 13 tables classified, ZERO orphaned AccessHarvester.exe/msaccess.exe; full AccessHarvester.Integration COM tier TRX-verified 56 passed / 1 skipped (the intentionally-guarded GoldenCorpusRegenerator dev tool) / 0 failed, 0 zombies. The 240s-timeout target test now passes in ~7s. Also fixes a real consumer-facing defect: classify (and other Access-backed subcommands) previously hung forever. Cross-provider session verification (gpt-5-4) returned VERIFIED round 1 across all five concerns (scoped-exit correctness, blast radius, E5 correctness, test-isolation safety, scope adherence) with zero issues; its sole non-issue maintainability caveat (a future in-process Program.Main caller could self-terminate) was documented in the flag's XML comment. Set closes here; the COM tier no longer carries an unexplained red. Orchestrated by Claude Code (Opus 4.8).

reason.specifics: This set is complete; the COM tier is green-or-skip.
